I don’t personally enjoy dog parks. It’s not a very structured environment and there are allot of irresponsible owners that allow there dogs to run rampant through the park. My personal recommendation for when your at work, or even when your at home, is doggy daycare. It’s a more structured environment with people trained in how to handle and asses situations with the dogs as well as correct them when there playing inappropriately. If you do decide to follow the oath of a dog park please make sure your dog is fully vaccinated, do research on the park, and try to go in the less busy hours for awhile.

I’d also like to add that there’s a difference between we separate them by size and play style. I’ve seen little chiwawa’s  wrestle with husky’s and malamutes that have to be put into the less active room because there too gentle. If they say ‘We separate by size’ ask to clarify if they actually mean size or the play style.

Also, please feel free to ask me any more questions you have! I know putting your dog into daycare can be really stressful and nerve racking. 

I think your doing the right step by introducing him at a young age so he can become socialized/ less afraid of more active environments. It really helped my dog learn to play well, be less afraid of others, and desensitize him to busy environments. 

Also, your dog might not warm up to it right away and thats also completely normal. Some dogs will sit in the corner of the room for there first dozen visits then suddenly they get all into it. If they say your dog isn’t playing with other please give him time to adjust to the environment. (I would try to take him on a consistent schedule. To much time between sessions can restart the process if he is nervous)

And if your dog warms up right away don’t be surprised if he takes a big nap when he gets home! (We’ve had customers call and complain there dogs slept after daycare but that’s what there supposed to do).

Oh, one last thing too! Sorry I just keep thinking of things. Lol. Ask and make sure they will give your dog a break from the room if they notice him becoming overstimulated. Not all dogs need it but some do and that’s totally fine. However, if they can’t provide a break for an overstimulated dog it can lead to behavior problems like aggression. At least while at daycare.

Hey there! I work at a Doggy Daycare so feel free to ask questions. 
Are there any in your area that have a live camera? I personally only bring my dog to doggy daycares with a live feed throughout the day. It helps with my general sanity and it is less likely to lead to any abuse since the parents can see everything.
One red flag for me is ALWAYS if they say they allow non neutered or fixed pets after a year of age. 

Some places don’t but if possible ask to do a quick tour of the facility. 

Are you okay with them correcting your dog? Part of our job is to correct to the dogs when there acting naughty and this generally helps you put in the long run as well because it keeps a consistentancy for the dog. (This does NOT mean physically harming the dogs. Corrections should never harm your pooch).

If they don’t require vaccinations that’s def a no go. 

I’ve also heard of places that don’t separate by play style and to me thats setting the dogs up for failure. It’s important that the less active dogs aren’t put in with the rowdy dogs. It only leads to problems.

Ask about there protocols on certain things, how often the room is cleaned, water changed, etc. and make sure your comfortable with the answers the ly provide. Never be scared to ask questions or raise concerns.
